Chapter 10: The Modern World—Technology, Change, and the Future of the Naked Ape.
Can you imagine how fast our world moves today, compared to the world of the very first naked apes? Back then, life moved at the pace of footsteps and fireside stories. Now, cities sprawl across continents, information zips around the globe in an instant, and somehow, we’re all more connected—and sometimes, more isolated—than ever before.
The challenges we face in modern life feel brand new, but the instincts that guide us? Those are ancient. They’ve shaped us since the beginning.
Technology’s transformed just about everything—how we talk, how we work, how we play, and even how we form relationships. Think about it: social media, smartphones, the internet. Sure, they help us connect, but they also bring a whole new set of stresses and worries. Most folks don’t realize that the way we behave online—chasing likes, joining groups, looking for approval—is powered by the same instincts that helped our ancestors survive on the savanna. We’re still looking for status, craving a sense of belonging, and needing to feel seen.
Picture someone scrolling through their phone late at night, searching for a spark of connection in a flood of updates and photos. That urge to belong—to be noticed and heard—it’s just as powerful now as it was thousands of years ago. Only now, the tools have changed, and so have the risks and rewards. The lines between public and private, what’s real and what’s virtual, are blurring every day, making life even more complicated for us naked apes.
With everything changing so quickly, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. Old ways of doing things disappear, and brand new possibilities pop up in their place. Lots of people struggle to keep up, feeling caught between what’s familiar and the excitement—or uncertainty—of what’s next. The skills that kept us alive in the past—like working together, being creative, and staying resilient—still matter, but now, we have to use them in ways our ancestors could never have imagined.
But here’s something amazing: the story of the naked ape is really a story of adapting. Time and again, we’ve faced challenges that seemed impossible. And time and again, we’ve found new ways to live, to love, and to thrive. Those old instincts that once kept us safe out in the wild? They’re still guiding us as we navigate the twists and turns of modern life.
So, what about the future? Well, it’s always going to be uncertain. But our ability to change—that’s unlimited. If we pay attention to where our behaviors really come from, we can discover new ways to connect, to create, and to make meaning in a world that never stops moving.
